sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol, marijuana and medication impairment, the open container law, under-21 zero tolerance, penalties for supplying alcohol to minors, aggressive driving, emotions and health, medical reporting to MVD, drowsy driving, and license revocation and reinstatement
Knowledge domain: how alcohol, marijuana, medications and illegal drugs impair a driver, what the open container law covers, what zero tolerance means for drivers under twenty-one, the license penalty for supplying alcohol to minors, when speeding becomes aggressive driving and how it is punished, how emotions, illness, medical conditions and fatigue affect driving, and how revocation and reinstatement work.

FACT_ID: sec18-F01 | anchor: A01
Keep a plan in mind for meeting a wrong-way driver, so you do not lose a moment taking evasive action that could save your life. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F02 | anchor: A01
Alcohol, marijuana, medications and illegal drugs do not mix with driving, and a driver who uses them can cause crashes, injuries and death. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F03 | anchor: A01
Driving demands the highest level of skill and judgment, and alcohol, marijuana, medications and illegal drugs all weaken both. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F04 | anchor: A01
Prescription drugs and over-the-counter allergy and cold medicines can impair your driving skills. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F05 | anchor: A01
Before you drive, always read medication labels for warnings about how the medicine may affect you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F06 | anchor: A01
Alcohol or drugs seriously reduce your reflexes, your physical control of the vehicle and your ability to recognize danger. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F07 | anchor: A01
Even when you do not look or feel impaired, alcohol or drugs give you a false sense of confidence in your driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F08 | anchor: A01
On any public roadway, neither a driver nor a passenger may drink from or possess an open container of spirituous liquor in the passenger compartment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F09 | anchor: A01
The open container rule does not apply to passengers in a bus, a limousine, a taxi or a motor home's living area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F10 | anchor: A01
For the open container rule, the passenger compartment includes any unlocked compartment or portable device within reach of the driver or a passenger. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F11 | anchor: A01
The trunk is outside the passenger compartment, and so is the space behind the rearmost upright seat when a vehicle has no trunk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F12 | anchor: A01
For drivers under 21, the manual's alcohol rule is zero tolerance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F13 | anchor: A01
After a first conviction for knowingly buying liquor for or giving it to a minor, the court may have MVD suspend the person's license for no more than 30 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F14 | anchor: A01
After a second or later conviction for supplying liquor to a minor, the suspension may last no more than six (6) months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F15 | anchor: A01
Young drivers are involved in crashes far more often than drivers in any other age group. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F16 | anchor: A01
Alcohol involvement in vehicle crashes is highest for people between the ages of 21 and 34. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-F17 | anchor: A02
Survey data shows that adults aged 21 to 29 are the most likely to drive after drinking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F18 | anchor: A02
Driving while impaired is a crime, and the consequences of driving under the influence are getting tougher. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F19 | anchor: A02
The surest way to avoid death, injury, penalties and jail is zero tolerance, which means no alcohol at all before driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F20 | anchor: A02
A driver under 21 with even a trace of an impairing substance, whether alcohol, marijuana, medication or an illegal drug, faces stiff penalties and a 2-year license suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F21 | anchor: A02
Being below the 0.08 blood alcohol concentration (BAC) legal limit does not make it legal or safe to drive, and a DUI arrest is still possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F22 | anchor: A02
Studies show that alcohol impairs driving at levels well below 0.08 BAC. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F23 | anchor: A02
You may be cited for aggressive driving if, during one continuous stretch of driving, you exceed the posted speed limit and commit two listed violations in a series of acts that is an immediate hazard to another person or vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F24 | anchor: A02
The violations that count toward aggressive driving are ignoring traffic control signs or signals, passing on the right, an unsafe lane change, following too closely and failing to yield to emergency vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F25 | anchor: A02
After a first aggressive driving offense you must complete Traffic Survival School, and a 30-day license suspension is possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F26 | anchor: A02
A second aggressive driving offense within 24 months is a Class 1 misdemeanor and brings a 12-month license suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F27 | anchor: A02
You cannot drive well when you are angry, excited, worried or depressed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F28 | anchor: A02
Anger is probably the emotion drivers feel most often, especially in heavy traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F29 | anchor: A02
Do not let your emotions shape your driving decisions, and wait until you are calm before you drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F30 | anchor: A02
Distracted driving may lead to crashes, injury or death. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F31 | anchor: A02
Your physical, mental and emotional condition matters more than any other problem you may meet on the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F32 | anchor: A02
Even a simple headache or a cold can affect your ability to drive safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F33 | anchor: A02
If you are ill, judge your fitness honestly and postpone the trip or let someone else drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-F34 | anchor: A03
Any condition that could affect your ability to drive safely must be reported to MVD. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F35 | anchor: A03
An applicant who had a seizure in the 90 days before applying for a license must report it to MVD. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F36 | anchor: A03
A licensed driver who has a seizure or another medical condition must stop driving, notify MVD and get a medical exam, and the physician sends the results to MVD. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F37 | anchor: A03
If you start feeling sleepy while driving, it is already past time to get off the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F38 | anchor: A03
Fatigue dulls the mind and weakens your ability to act quickly and correctly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F39 | anchor: A03
Five groups are known to be at higher crash risk from sleepiness: shift workers, business travelers, commercial drivers, people with sleep disorders and young people. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F40 | anchor: A03
Drowsy driving is as serious and dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol, but it is harder to detect. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F41 | anchor: A03
Rest is the only safe remedy for driver fatigue. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F42 | anchor: A03
To avoid fatigue, rest well before a long trip and avoid driving late at night. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F43 | anchor: A03
Take frequent rest stops where you get out of the vehicle, exercise, breathe deeply and move around. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F44 | anchor: A03
Avoid a fixed forward stare by shifting your eyes often and glancing at the mirrors and gauges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F45 | anchor: A03
Open the windows for fresh air, sing along with the radio or chew gum, and change drivers often if you can. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F46 | anchor: A03
Driver Improvement is the process of finding drivers who are not driving responsibly and either correcting their behavior or taking away their privilege to drive in Arizona. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F47 | anchor: A03
Revocation is the removal of your driving privilege, and the law requires it after conviction for certain driving offenses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F48 | anchor: A03
When a revocation period ends, your privilege stays revoked until an investigation confirms that every withdrawal action has ended and all statutory requirements are met. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F49 | anchor: A03
To reinstate after a revocation you pay the application fee and a $20 reinstatement fee, and you may have to file a Certificate of Insurance, commonly called an SR-22. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-F50 | anchor: A03
After a revocation, MVD may require you to take a written, vision and road test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

Misconceptions: staying under the legal blood alcohol limit does not make driving legal or safe; over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines can impair you too; the trunk is outside the passenger compartment, but an unlocked compartment within reach is inside it; a revoked privilege does not return by itself when the period ends; gum, the radio and fresh air may help you stay alert, but only rest cures fatigue.
Mnemonics: Under twenty-one, zero means zero; aggressive driving is speeding plus two; sleepy means you are already late to stop.
Glossary: blood alcohol concentration means the share of alcohol in the blood, written as BAC; open container means an opened container of spirituous liquor; revocation means the removal of the driving privilege; SR-22 means a Certificate of Insurance filed to prove coverage; Traffic Survival School means the driver course required after a first aggressive driving offense.
Dynamic facts: impaired-driving penalties, the aggressive driving penalties, the minor-supply suspensions and the reinstatement fee are statutory or set by MVD and can change.
